captions.text: Open Personnel to manage the people in your department.
The top actions include Add a Person, Manage Invites and Manage Roles.
This walkthrough uses Add a Person to create a fictional member directly.
Peter Mills will join a community coordination group with a
community response navigator role.
Choosing the member’s group, operational role and department access deliberately
helps the roster reflect the work that person is expected to do.

scenes.title: Enter unique account credentials

captions.text: Under Account Information, enter a unique Username.
Enter a New Password and the matching Confirm Password.
The help here requires at least eight characters, including a digit, an
required_labels: Passwords must be 8 characters or longer and include a digit (number), an uppercase and lowercase letter

captions.text: uppercase letter and a lowercase letter.
The example keeps both password fields masked.
Review the actual requirements on your form and use a separate
credential for the member.
The username identifies the account; the profile details below identify
the person on the department roster.

visual_required_labels: The User Name must be unique

captions.text: In User Details, enter the member’s I D Number, First Name,
Last Name and Email Address.
This fictional example uses Peter Mills and a training-only identification number.
The email help says Email Addresses must be unique.
Use the intended person’s correct details in your own department so that the saved
profile and roster are recognizable.
These identity fields are separate from the group and role selections that follow.

scenes.title: Choose a group and operational role

captions.text: Under Group Details, choose the community coordination training group.
Leave Is Group Admin unchecked for this example.
Under Roles, select the community response navigator training role.
The selected role appears as a chip in the field.
Group membership, group administration and a personnel role have separate controls.
Assign the operational role the member needs, then decide separately whether
the person should administer the group.
This exercise keeps that administration checkbox clear.

scenes.title: Review account notification and password-change choices

captions.text: At the bottom, review Notify User and Require Password Change.
The first note says to uncheck Notify User if you do not want Resgrid to notify
the person of this account creation.
It is unchecked for our local training example.
Require Password Change is a separate first-login choice,
and remains unchecked here.
Review those choices before selecting Add Person.
This lesson creates the account without demonstrating a notification delivery
or a first-login password change.
After Add Person, the saved Personnel list can be filtered with Search.
Search for Peter Mills and check the matching row.
It shows the community response navigator role and a Normal state.
Staffing is Available and Status is Standing By in this exercise.
Read those separate columns instead of assuming that a normal account
state describes the person’s current operational availability.
Select Edit on this row to review the saved profile.

scenes.title: Review and change the profile time zone

captions.text: The reopened profile contains the saved identity fields.
Review Time Zone as well.
In this example the initial selection is Hawaii, which does not match the
intended Chicago training context.
Change it to Central Time, U S and Canada.

spoken_references.(GMT-06:00) Central Time (US & Canada): Central Time, U S and Canada

captions.text: Selecting the option prepares a change; it is not saved yet.
Continue to the bottom of the profile, where the same Save action will store
this time-zone change together with the department settings we review next.
Under Department Settings, keep User Type set to Normal User rather
than selecting Department Admin.
Check Disable User and leave Hide User clear, then select Save.
Back in Personnel, Peter’s saved State now reads Normal, Disabled.
The row still shows Available under Staffing and Standing By under Status.
That visible result is why account-state controls and operational staffing or
status should be reviewed separately.
This recording verifies the saved disabled state, without
attempting a sign-in as Peter.

scenes.title: Clear the disabled state and verify it

captions.text: Reopen Edit for the same member.
Keep Normal User selected, clear Disable User, leave Hide User
unchecked, and select Save.
Search for Peter again.
The saved State now reads Normal, and the community response
navigator role remains on the row.
This readback confirms the department-state change was stored.
Use the same review-and-save approach when an authorized administrator needs to
change a member’s department access, and check the result on the intended person.

scenes.title: Confirm the retained profile and apply the pattern

captions.text: Reopening the profile also confirms that Central Time, the
community coordination group and the navigator role were retained.
Is Group Admin remains clear.
The same member setup applies beyond fire and E M S.
Community paramedicine and mental health teams can organize coordinators;
search-and-rescue and security departments can organize field personnel; wildland
contractors and industrial emergency teams can organize their crews.
Use your own group and role names, review the access settings, save, and
verify the resulting member profile.
